newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's Meridor says interest rates too high.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Meridor says interest rates too high.

text.p: Israeli Finance Minister Dan Meridor said on Tuesday that interest rates are still high, despite the cut announced on Monday.

"There is no doubt that interest rates in Israel are high and that the nominal rate are still around 15 percent. Expected inflation in coming months is apparently around eight percent or even less," Meridor told Israel Radio. "Therefore real interest rates are very high."
On Monday, the Bank of Israel said it would be lowering the base rate 0.5 percentage point to 14.2 percent, which was in line with expectations.

The central bank has been under pressure to cut rates more sharply as inflation has fallen in the last six months and high rates have put upward pressure on the shekel exchange rate. But Meridor indicated he would not welcome a drastic cut.
"I oppose sharp measures. Every measure has to be moderate and considered. Perhaps interest rates should not be changed once a month but rather once a week or once a day."
